land.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Lê court's north (Thanh Hóa, Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh) under the Trịnh lords

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established: 1545' (Trịnh Kiểm at the head of the Lê court, 1545-1570) and predecessors Mạc dynasty and Revival Lê dynasty. Cliopatria's Lê row ends in 1571 and this row begins in 1572 on the same land, so the map separates the two in 1572; the lords governed the Lê court's north earlier.

land.text: the north (Tonkin), taken by the Tây Sơn after the Trịnh fell

successors.note: Infobox successor: Tây Sơn dynasty. Trịnh Bồng 'was defeated by Chỉnh in fall 1787' (Trịnh lords page): Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh ruled the north for the Lê emperor until Nguyễn Huệ returned; Cliopatria's Tây Sơn shape reaches the north in 1788. Lê Chiêu Thống (1786-1788) is the emperor who fled.

capitals.name: Tây Đô (Thanh Hóa)
capitals.note: The page says Tây Đô was 'founded as a temporary capital' while Đông Kinh was in Mạc hands; it gives no years. The span is bridged from the 1592 retaking of the capital.

capitals.name: Đông Kinh (Hanoi)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Đông Kinh'; the capital 'was retaken in 1592'. The Lê emperor Thế Tông returned to Đông Kinh in April 1593 (Lê-Mạc War page). The Tây Sơn took Thăng Long in 1786 and withdrew (Quang Trung page).

rulers.name: Trịnh Tùng
rulers.title: lord (chúa)
rulers.note: Page table 1570-1623 (the infobox gives 1572 as king); his father Trịnh Kiểm ruled 1545-1570 and Trịnh Cối six months in 1570. The Lê emperors are not listed.

rulers.name: Trịnh Tông
rulers.title: lord (chúa)
rulers.note: Committed suicide in 1786 when the Tây Sơn took Thăng Long (Trịnh lords page).

rulers.name: Trịnh Bồng
rulers.title: lord (chúa)
rulers.note: Defeated by Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh in fall 1787, ending Trịnh rule. The page says twelve lords but its table lists thirteen names.

correction.text: shape unchanged; applies 1572-1591 only, because Đông Kinh and the delta are Trịnh land from 1592, not 1595 (new keyframe trinh-lords_1592)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: applies 1572-1591. 45,835 km2, 150 cells: Thanh Hóa (37 of 41 cells), Nghệ An (54 of 62) and Hà Tĩnh (17 of 19), none of the delta; the page says only that the Mạc 'remained at large in the north' after the 1533 Lê restoration and puts the retaking of the capital in 1592 (Trịnh lords page) while the Mạc page has the Trịnh holding the capital for a year from 1572. The page gives no area, so no infobox check.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1595 outline (353 cells, Red River delta and the north without Cao Bằng) for 1592-1594: the Lê-Trịnh reconquest of Đông Kinh and the northern provinces

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1592-1594 on Cliopatria's 1595 outline. 'conquered Hanoi along with the rest of the northern provinces' in 1592 (Mạc dynasty page); infobox 'Đông Kinh (1527-1592)'. The Lê-Mạc War page has the Lê emperor Thế Tông 'welcomed back to Đông Kinh' in April 1593. Cliopatria shows the delta as Trịnh only from 1595, three years late.

103,059 km2 (353 cells at 253 km2) for 1595-1644: the delta and the north, with Cao Bằng left out: the shape does not overlap the 36-cell Cao Bằng outline of Đại Việt 1595, the Mạc rump that 'withdrew to Cao Bằng' and survived to 1677 (Lê-Mạc War page; the Mạc page gives it 1593-1625 under Mạc Kính Cung and a Ming commission of 1598 'declared the Mạc to be rulers over Cao Bằng'). The page gives no area.
1645-1647: the same 103,059 km2 outline as 1595; the pages dated no change on the Trịnh frontiers in these years (the Cliopatria split follows the Ming, Southern Ming and Qing neighbours).
1648-1652: 103,087 km2, a cell more than 1645. The page has the Royal army 'badly beaten' at Trường Dục in 1648 by the Nguyễn, with no change of frontier.

correction.text: shape unchanged; applies 1653-1655, the Nguyễn occupation of Hà Tĩnh; from 1656 the 1659 outline (new keyframe trinh-lords_1656)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: applies 1653-1655. The Cliopatria outline (95,947 km2) lacks Hà Tĩnh (0 of 19 cells) and two Nghệ An cells: 'The Nguyễn invaded the north and captured Quảng Bình, then Hà Tĩnh' in 1653 and attacked Nghệ An in 1654, where the Trịnh under Trịnh Tạc counterattacked and defeated them; by 1656 'the Nguyễn were pushed back to their original walls' (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page), so the land is Trịnh again from 1656, not 1659.

correction.text: the 1659 outline (103,087 km2) for 1656-1658: Hà Tĩnh back under the Trịnh after the Nguyễn were pushed back to their original walls

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1656-1658 on the 1659 outline: the Nguyễn 'were pushed back to their original walls' in 1656; Cliopatria keeps them in Hà Tĩnh until 1658.

1659-1676: 103,087 km2. The 1661 attack on the walls failed; the 1671 offensive of 80,000 men was halted by the Nguyễn navy. The frontier here is Cliopatria's line (southern edge 17.96 N), about 9 cells north of the Gianh River that the page gives as the de facto border: Quảng Bình is left wholly to the Nguyễn. The page does not date when the Gianh became the line, so the strip is left as drawn.

1677-1708: 113,217 km2, the 1659 outline plus Cao Bằng (39 cells, 22 of them Cao Bằng province): 'The Mạc in Cao Bằng were completely defeated by the Trịnh clan in 1677' and the remnants 'were annexed and exiled to China' (Lê-Mạc War page). Seven of its cells fall across the Chinese border (five already in the 1659 outline); the pages dated no frontier with the Qing, to whom the Trịnh sent tribute, so they are read as border-cell artefacts.

1709-1712: 113,384 km2, the 1677 outline within a cell or two. No territorial change is dated on the Trịnh page between 1677 and 1774; it mentions a 1694 war in Laos and Lao kingdoms paying tribute to both Vietnam and Siam about a decade later, without land.
1713-1756: 113,329 km2, unchanged from 1709 within a cell; no dated event on the page.
1757-1761: 113,274 km2, unchanged within a cell; no dated event on the page.
1762-1774: 113,329 km2; the frontier is the 1673 line, 'strongly guarded but peaceful' for about a hundred years, until 15 November 1774 (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page).

correction.text: the Trịnh north (1778 outline) plus Thuận Hóa as the Trịnh viceroyalty from early 1775; Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and Bình Định are Nguyễn Nhạc's client land (ledger vassal events), the upland beyond is dropped

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1775-1777. Cliopatria's 158,296 km2 runs to 13.5 N and takes in Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi, Bình Định (35, 17 and 21 cells) and 59 cells of upland beyond them. The pages give the Trịnh the capital Phú Xuân (Huế) 'in the next year' after 1774 and make Hoàng Ngũ Phúc 'viceroy of Thuận Hóa' (Hoàng Ngũ Phúc page), while 'Nguyễn Nhạc was made an official of the Trịnh lords' (Quang Trung page): the Trịnh held Thuận Hóa directly and Nhạc's Quảng Nam as a client, drawn as a tint through the vassal events, not as direct land.

correction.text: the northern outline plus Thuận Hóa (Quảng Bình, Quảng Trị, Huế), held by the Trịnh viceroy Bùi Thế Đạt after Hoàng Ngũ Phúc's death in 1776

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1778-1782. Cliopatria returns to the 113,329 km2 northern outline in 1778, the year the Tây Sơn page has Nhạc proclaim himself emperor, and gives Huế to the Tây Sơn (16 of 17 cells). The Hoàng Ngũ Phúc page: Phúc, viceroy of Thuận Hóa, died on his way back to Phú Xuân and 'Bùi Thế Đạt was appointed as his successor'; the Quang Trung page has Huệ march 'north to attack Phú Xuân' only in 1786. Thuận Hóa therefore stays Trịnh to 1786 (confidence 2: the pages never say 'the Trịnh held Phú Xuân until 1786').

correction.text: the northern outline plus Thuận Hóa; applies 1783-1785

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1783-1785 with Thuận Hóa as in 1778; 1786-1787 is the northern outline alone (new keyframe trinh-lords_1786): in 1786 'an army under Nguyễn Huệ, Vũ Văn Nhậm and Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh marched north to attack Phú Xuân' and then took Thăng Long (Quang Trung page).

correction.text: the northern outline (113,329 km2) for 1786-1787, without Thuận Hóa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1786-1787: Thuận Hóa gone to the Tây Sơn; the Trịnh keep the north. After Huệ left, 'the regime of Trịnh lord restored' (Quang Trung page) under Trịnh Bồng, who fell to Chỉnh in fall 1787 (Trịnh lords page).

region.text: Thanh Hóa, Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh, the Trịnh base

ledger.note: 1572: the Trịnh lords stand at the head of the Lê court's north. Infobox 'Established: 1545'; Trịnh Kiểm 1545-1570; Trịnh Tùng 1570-1623 in the page table, with 1572 in the infobox as the year he became king; the lords governed for the Lê emperors (the sibling le-dynasty dossier calls them rulers in name only). The map separates them from the Lê in 1572, the year Cliopatria and the Lê dossier hand over.

region.text: Thăng Long (Đông Kinh), the Mạc capital

ledger.note: 1572: the Trịnh take Thăng Long. 'In 1572 the capital was captured by the Trịnh army but then he recaptured it a year later.' Hatched: Mạc land held for a year, not annexed.
1573: the Mạc retake the capital 'a year later' (Mạc dynasty page); the page has no month.

region.text: the delta around Đông Kinh and Hải Dương, fought over in 1592

ledger.note: 1592: the Lê-Trịnh army marches on Đông Kinh. The page dates the reconquest to 1592: 'Đông Kinh, the capital of the Mạc dynasty, was reconquered by the Later Lê forces' and on 25 November 1592 Trịnh Tùng's forces arrested and executed Mạc Mậu Hợp at Hải Dương. The page gives no month for the campaign's start.

region.text: the delta and the north outside Cao Bằng: the 1595 outline without the 1572 core (204 cells)

ledger.note: 1592: Đông Kinh and the northern provinces pass from the Mạc to the Trịnh-led Lê court. The Mạc page: the Trịnh invasion 'conquered Hanoi along with the rest of the northern provinces'; the Lê-Mạc War page adds that 'the Mạc remnants fled to the mountainous Bắc Cạn, Cao Bằng provinces'. Cliopatria shows the gain from 1595.

1592: the capital returns to Đông Kinh (Hanoi). The page: the capital 'was retaken in 1592', Tây Đô having been 'founded as a temporary capital'; the emperor Thế Tông was welcomed back to Đông Kinh in April 1593 (Lê-Mạc War page).

region.text: the delta, now held by the Lê-Trịnh

ledger.note: April 1593: the Lê emperor returns to Đông Kinh. 'In April 1593, the southern emperor Lê Thế Tông was welcomed back to Đông Kinh (Hanoi)'; the fighting then shrinks to the Mạc rump in Cao Bằng.

region.text: Hà Tĩnh, taken by the Nguyễn after Quảng Bình

ledger.note: 1653: the Nguyễn invade the north. 'The Nguyễn invaded the north and captured Quảng Bình, then Hà Tĩnh'; in 1654 they attacked Nghệ An and Trịnh Tạc's counterattack defeated them.

region.text: Hà Tĩnh, recovered when the Nguyễn were pushed back to their walls

ledger.note: 1656: the Nguyễn are 'pushed back to their original walls' and Hà Tĩnh returns to the Trịnh. The page gives 1656 without naming the province; Cliopatria keeps the Nguyễn there until 1658.

region.text: Cao Bằng, the Mạc rump state of 1592-1677

ledger.note: 1677: the Trịnh destroy the Mạc rump in Cao Bằng. 'The Mạc in Cao Bằng were completely defeated by the Trịnh clan in 1677' and the remnants 'were annexed and exiled to China'; the Mạc page has Mạc Kính Vũ fleeing into Guangxi after the Battle of Cao Bình (1677).

region.text: the Nguyễn walls north of Huế and the land behind them

ledger.note: 15 November 1774: Trịnh Sâm attacks the Nguyễn and, 'for the first time', the Nguyễn walls are broken, ending a truce of about a hundred years (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page).

region.text: Quảng Nam and the Tây Sơn land to the south, held by Nguyễn Nhạc as a Trịnh official

ledger.note: 1775: Nguyễn Nhạc becomes a Trịnh official. 'The proposal was accepted, and Nguyễn Nhạc was made an official of the Trịnh lords' after the Trịnh army crossed the Hải Vân Pass and defeated the Tây Sơn in Quảng Nam; the Hoàng Ngũ Phúc page has Nhạc 'turn to swear allegiance to Trịnh lord' after his defeat at Cẩm Sa. The page gives no date beyond 1775; the provinces are my reading of Nhạc's Quảng Nam base.

February 1775: the Trịnh take Huế. 'February 1775: The Trịnh captured Huế, the Nguyễn capital'; after fighting with the Tây Sơn 'a treaty was signed and the Trịnh left the destruction of the Nguyễn to the southern rebels'.

region.text: Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces

ledger.note: 1775: Thuận Hóa passes to a Trịnh viceroy. 'In the next year, Trịnh army occupied Phú Xuân (modern Huế)'; Phúc 'was appointed viceroy of Thuận Hóa by Trịnh Sâm'. The Trịnh lords page has the Trịnh withdraw in mid-1775 because of plague 'leaving the south to the Tây Sơn', which the Hoàng Ngũ Phúc page (Bùi Thế Đạt succeeds Phúc) and the 1786 march on Phú Xuân (Quang Trung page) contradict for Thuận Hóa; the three provinces are my reading of 'Thuận Hóa'.

region.text: the Tây Sơn land of Nguyễn Nhạc

ledger.note: 1778: Nguyễn Nhạc proclaims himself emperor ('Nguyễn Nhạc, proclaimed himself Emperor in 1778'), ending his place as a Trịnh official. The page does not say so in words; Cliopatria returns the middle country to the Tây Sơn in 1778.

region.text: Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces

ledger.note: 1786: the Tây Sơn take Phú Xuân. 'An army under Nguyễn Huệ, Vũ Văn Nhậm and Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh marched north to attack Phú Xuân'; the Trịnh lords page has Nhạc order the attack in summer 1786. The page gives no month for Phú Xuân.

1787: the Trịnh lords end. 'Trịnh Bồng was defeated by Chỉnh in fall 1787, ending Trịnh rule'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1787'. Chỉnh's northern regime for the Lê emperor Lê Chiêu Thống fell to the Tây Sơn in 1788.

wars.name: Lê–Mạc War

zones.text: the Mạc offensive of 1570-1572 down to the Cả River
Cao Bằng, the Mạc rump to 1677

wars.outcome: Revival Lê and Trịnh victory: Đông Kinh reconquered in 1592, the Mạc rump in Cao Bằng 'completely defeated by the Trịnh clan in 1677'.
wars.note: The page dates the war 1533-1593 and 1593-1677. 'In August 1570, Mạc Kính Điển launched a large southward offensive'; 'In 1571, Mạc forces advanced further south to Cả River'; 'In October 1572, Mạc forces retreated back to the north'. The Trịnh span from 1572 only.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (first phase)

zones.text: the Nguyễn walls near Đồng Hới, north of Huế
Hà Tĩnh, held by the Nguyễn 1653-1655

wars.outcome: Indecisive: open warfare from 1627, offensives in 1633, 1642-43, 1648, 1661 and 1671 failed against the walls; the Nguyễn invaded in 1653 and were pushed back by 1656; peace in 1673 'mediated by the Kangxi Emperor's government' with the Linh River as the border.
wars.note: The infobox dates the phase 1627-1672 and the text has the peace in 1673; the page gives the Gianh River as the de facto line in peacetime and the Linh River as the 1673 border.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (second phase)
wars.outcome: Trịnh and Tây Sơn victory: the Trịnh captured Phú Xuân in February 1775 and the Nguyễn retreated to Quảng Nam and later to Gia Định; the Trịnh left the destruction of the Nguyễn to the southern rebels.
wars.note: Infobox 'Date: 15 November 1774-1775'; 'Territorial changes: Trịnh captured Phú Xuân in 1775'.

wars.name: Tây Sơn campaign against the Trịnh
wars.outcome: Tây Sơn victory: Phú Xuân and Thăng Long fell in 1786, Trịnh Tông died and the lords were restored only briefly under Trịnh Bồng, who fell to Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh in fall 1787.
wars.note: Banner 'Destroy the Trịnh and Aid the Lê' (Trịnh lords page). The Quang Trung page gives no month for Phú Xuân or Thăng Long.

certainty.note: The Mạc front, the Cham-Nguyễn walls and the Lao and Chinese uplands are approximate.

The southern frontier with the Nguyễn is the line of the 1673 peace ('strongly guarded but peaceful'; the Gianh or Linh River) and is the one sharp border, but the Cao Bằng, Lao and Qing frontiers stay soft, so the era is soft.
The Thuận Hóa viceroyalty and Nhạc's client land have no stated lines.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 14 shapes, all reviewed; three new keyframes (1592, 1656, 1786). The Trịnh page gives no area, so the infobox check could not be made; shapes are compared with the pages' places instead.
Mirrors of sibling ledgers: ai-viet (Mạc) has the 1572-1573 occupation of Thăng Long, the 1592 contest and loss, April 1593, and the 1677 loss of Cao Bằng; nguyen-lords carries the 1653 invasion and 1656 return and the 1774-1775 contest. Counterparts not yet written by their groups: tay-son-dynasty (vassal events 1775-1778, loss of Thuận Hóa in 1786, successor), le-dynasty (written, ends 1571).
Main correction: Cliopatria draws the Trịnh with the whole middle country (Quảng Nam to Bình Định) in 1775-1777 and then without Thuận Hóa from 1778. The pages support Thuận Hóa as a Trịnh viceroyalty (Hoàng Ngũ Phúc, then Bùi Thế Đạt) to Huệ's 1786 attack and Nhạc's land as a client of the Trịnh from 1775 to 1778; the Trịnh lords page's 'withdrew ... leaving the south to the Tây Sơn' is the one contrary statement. Confidence 2 because no page says the Trịnh held Phú Xuân until 1786.
Months not on the pages: the 1592 campaign start, 1786 Phú Xuân and Thăng Long (the brief's June/July 1786 are not on the Quang Trung or Tây Sơn pages), the Tây Sơn occupation of Thăng Long and its end in 1786 (not drawn), the end of Trịnh Bồng in fall 1787.
Undated on the pages: when the Gianh became the frontier (Cliopatria's line is about 9 cells north of it, left as drawn); the Trịnh involvement in a 1694 war in Laos and Lao tribute to Vietnam and Siam (Trịnh page, no land; Lan Xang and its successors are another batch's); the Qing frontier (seven Cliopatria cells in China, read as artefacts).
Page conflicts: Mạc retreat to Cao Bằng 1592 (infobox) against 1593-1625 (Mạc Kính Cung); Phú Xuân 'the next year' (Hoàng Ngũ Phúc) against February 1775 (Trịnh-Nguyễn War) against 'early 1775' (Trịnh lords); the 1673 Linh River border against the Gianh River as de facto line (same page); Trịnh Tùng from 1570 or 1572; twelve lords in the text and thirteen in the table. The Trịnh page also says the Qing intervened in 1537, an anachronism.
